searchText: In the real world, different layers are doing each of these things. `estimateGas`, for example, is often done by the application because they may need to add some padding that only they have the context to know about. `maxFeePerGas` on the other hand really needs to be done by the wallet based on prioritization information from the user+app. `transactionCount` also should be done by the wallet, not the node, because a user may have multiple transactions queuing up and the node may not have seen them all yet (especially if the intent is to bundle the transactions together). In other words, the Ethereum client doesn't have enough information to correctly fill out transactions in all cases, but there are some pieces that only it can do (gas estimation).
